page: Amazon Web Services r6i.12xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro System and 3rd Generation Intel Xeon Scalable processors (Ice Lake 8375C). Operating on an x86_64 architecture, the platform provides 48 dedicated vCPUs derived from 24 physical cores with multithreading enabled, reaching speeds up to 3.5 GHz. The configuration is provisioned with 384 GB of DDR4 memory clocked at 3000 MHz, maintaining an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. The instance does not bundle local NVMe storage, relying instead on network-attached storage, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 19 Gbps. Hardware acceleration via discrete GPUs is not present.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate competitive general compute performance, including a PassMark CPU score of 48,391.39 and a Geekbench multi-core rating of 15,739.0. Cryptographic throughput is an operational highlight, evidenced by a top-quartile PassMark CPU encryption score of 43,366.49, bolstered by hardware AVX-512 and VAES vector instruction flags. Memory tests register uncached sequential read speeds of 163.34 GB/s and write speeds of 69.82 GB/s, enabling the instance to achieve 45.38 million operations per second during Redis SET testing. Conversely, compute tasks that require massive parallel acceleration reveal limitations: large language model text generation on a 70B parameter model falls into the lower 25% at 2.68 tokens per second.

By delivering high memory density per core, the r6i.12xlarge offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound workloads that do not demand proportional compute or hardware GPU accelerators. The lack of integrated ephemeral storage requires consideration of external storage latency and I/O costs. This server profile is appropriately aligned with in-memory caching frameworks, relational and NoSQL databases, memory-heavy analytics pipelines, and distributed data processing tiers.

The instance delivers 48 dedicated vCPUs across 24 physical cores clocked up to 3.5 GHz alongside 384 GB of DDR4 memory, maintaining an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU allocation ratio. It includes 19 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, operates without bundled local NVMe storage, and contains no dedicated GPUs. Lacking onboard storage and specialized accelerators, the r6i.12xlarge provides resource efficiency targeted directly at large-footprint in-memory databases, distributed caching layers, data mining, and memory-intensive enterprise transaction processing.
